title: Asset Depletion Loan Requirements: Mortgage With No Income
description: How an asset depletion loan turns your savings into income for a mortgage, what counts, typical requirements, and why some lenders divide by 60 months, not 360.
h1: Asset Depletion Loans: How to Get a Mortgage With No Income
dek: Retired, between jobs or living off investments? Your savings can count as income.

faq.q: What is an asset depletion loan?
faq.a: An asset depletion loan is a mortgage where the lender turns your savings and investments into a monthly income figure, so you can qualify without a paycheck. It suits retirees and people who sold a business.

faq.q: How is asset depletion income calculated?
faq.a: The lender takes your eligible assets, subtracts the down payment, closing costs and required reserves, and divides the rest by a set number of months. Fannie Mae uses the months in the loan, 360 for a 30-year mortgage. Some lenders divide by fewer months; one we work with divides by 60.

faq.q: Can I get a mortgage with no income but assets?
faq.a: Yes. With an asset depletion loan, your savings and investments can stand in for income. You'll need enough assets left after the purchase, and the money usually needs to have been in your account for a few months.

faq.q: Do retirement accounts count for asset depletion?
faq.a: Yes, usually at part of their value. One of our lenders counts 70% of a retirement account if you are 59½ or older and 60% if you are younger. That lender counts cash in checking or savings in full.

sources.name: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.4-06, Employment-Related Assets as Qualifying Income
